lines.text: This is Reticle. Images that are circuits. On TapeOut, a circuit is a hex blob nobody can see. Reticle turns that blob into a picture you can draw, and read back from the chain.
Draw an icon on a sixteen by sixteen grid. As you paint, the compiler turns each pixel column into NAND gates, and shows the gate count against a naive netlist. This one ends up at sixty gates.
Connect OKX Wallet. The cost is read from the chain: thirty millionths of an OKB of ink per gate, plus the tapeout fee.
Two confirmations. One mints the ink. One tapes the circuit out.

Each gate burns one Reticle transistor. Then the page reads the circuit back from X Layer, one row at a time, and checks every pixel against the drawing. Two hundred fifty six of two hundred fifty six match.
Circuit eleven is live. The same page gives you the embed: one script tag and one image tag. No wallet, no gas for the viewer. The image is drawn by the chain's own gates.
On the X Layer explorer, the tapeout minted circuit eleven and burned sixty transistors, one per gate.
You can also download the SVG or PNG, a thirty two pixel favicon, or a share card. Nine seed circuits verify pixel exact, through direct eval and through our on-chain renderer.
Reticle. Images that are circuits. Live on X Layer. Contracts are TapeOut upgradeable beacons, unaudited.
